questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that to me, that I choose a location, where I could improve my language skills, and also be close to my friends :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too hard, but it did help looking at the Korean sites instead of the English ones, as the pages didn't exactly hold the same answers.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I dont know if i received assistance per say, however the Office of International Affairs was pretty helpful and sent out the necessary information. Otherwise, asking people around me and the people working in the buildings always helped.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We were housed in the International student dorms. It was the only dorm that wasn't directly ON campus, so the walk to class would be between 5-10 min. We were housed next to the high school, so there were usually a lot of students around.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen in another building, where there were fridges, cooking appliances, and stovetops. However, I personally only used the microwave, as the kitchen was always filled with people which made it overstimulating...

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of stuff you need to buy for the dorm - from cleaning supplies to bedding. Its also a good idea to buy some food (instant rice, ramen, snacks), that you can easily prepare with hot water or a microwave. Since there is a curfew at 1 am, and you cant leave nor enter at that time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it was just a bunch of mails and excel sheets. At times pretty overwhelming but if you talked it through with people going to the same uni, then it was fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get provided with a 'buddy'. The buddy is there to help with any questions you may have. There was also the Office of International Affairs, they usually answered pretty quickly on mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted, so that was pretty nice. However, my friend helped me register since it was pretty confusing... I think i registered one or two classes myself. It's just good to know that they only open registration a certain number at a time, so you have to keep trying every day..

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you are to stay at the dorms, then prepare to deep clean! 
Join clubs! Its a great way to meet locals and other exchange students. 
Apply to the events that the OIA offers.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I think the courses were pretty straight forward. I had two Korean classes and two in English.
You have freedom choosing courses so I had a barista course in Korean, and then some culture classes in English as well as Korean.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I feel like it was very hands on in some classes. Lots of presentations and public speaking, so that's something you have to be comfortable with or would like to challenge yourself with. I only had written assignments like twice and those were in my Korean classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
바리스타실무 
한국사회의이슈와쟁점
AI in the ages of philosophy
Hallyu and Pop culture media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think my coffee making class was really entertaining. However, I do recommend being able to speak Korean otherwise it will be hard to understand the teacher. The AI class was also interesting and quite informing. The teacher was also really engaging and enlightening.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had some hospital visits, and a lot of pharmacy visits - so I spent a good deal on medicine and hospital bills.. lol

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is less expensive in general (compared to Denmark). Public transport also isn't too bad - you can get pretty far on 200kr a month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There's a lot of clubs that you can join - albeit not every club wants exchange students.
There's also a lot of events for exchange students only via OIA that get mailed to you.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend exploring the area, as well as going on the Chuncheon City Tour. 
Clubs - I was in the Archery Club as well as the English Club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Nami Island, the surrounding nature, Han River, Seoul in general, Daegu, Busan, Jeju, Daejeon?? 
There's a lot. But just try to explore. Walking - do lots of it!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy. There wasn't like BIG culture shocks. But they do appreciate manners as well as being polite.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Clubs! Find people that are either good at english or that you wish to improve your own language skills with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
If you have dietary restrictions, you may experience some hardships. Sometimes, it doesn't say that there's gonna be pork or whatever in what you are ordering, but when it comes out - all of a sudden you can't eat it bc of it.
So asking is always a good idea.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the small conversations and the politeness of interacting with store workers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try new things, challenge yourself, and have fun ??

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Learn how the bank works - the one on campus. Before you get your ARC that place will become your best friend

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing my skills improve and the friends I made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being social (if you're not used to it) and being a 'foreigner' in a different country. Things are different from what one is used to in their home country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
